gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-numans: Floaty, friendly letters with room to spare. Nasalization does best at spacing out big, open display shapes, while Numans, a sans with hanging s ends, does best at wide-tracked running text.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Noto Sans Khudawadi keeps capitals and lowercase close in height. Neon does best at glowing, stylus-wide display lines, while Noto Sans Khudawadi does best at unlatched, quietly open rounds.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-modi: Glow up top, daylight below. Neon's uniform-width lines sit above Noto Sans Modi's daylight-filled curves, and that stark shift from glowing to open is the standout feature.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-multani: Hot, humming letters with nothing thin about them. Noto Sans Multani does best at lofty lowercase with a gaping e, while Neon does best at display lines with full-width joins.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-newa: Vibrant, humming display lines that never once thin out. Noto Sans Newa, with an open-mouthed e and tall bowls, keeps paragraphs feeling modern, readable and crisp, line after line.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-pathway-extreme: Marker-nib glow over stubby, sturdy lowercase. Neon's direction-blind line meets Pathway Extreme's big x-height and clear round openings, and that jump from glow to openness is the main draw.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-radio-canada: Bright tubes of light over tidy, upright type. Neon does best at glowing display lines of one width, while Radio Canada, with c, s and z standing tall and full, does best at steady text.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-sono: Glowing monoline caps over loose, wide-set text. What stands out is openness: Neon's true monoline strokes breathe, and Sono's wide spacing and ajar a's do the same in text.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-carrois-got: Pulled-apart letters with a neon-tube hum. Neuropolitical does best at cut-out, router-bit display shapes, while Carrois Gothic SC does best at near-uniform capital and lowercase heights and clear curve endings.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-hind-vadoda: Stretched-out letters, glowing like neon tubes. Neuropolitical does best at geometric, pulled-apart display words, while Hind Vadodara, with spacious terminal gaps and tall bowls, does best at unhurried text.
